specification.objective: Clarify the active selection in the Memory/User and Pending writes/Stored memory segmented selectors using one shared visual language without altering behavior, compact layout or backend.

requirements.statement: Both selectors reuse the same UI component and show selected choice with a high-visibility accent outline, elevated background, persistent indicator and stronger text; inactive choices have separate hover appearance.
Each option remains a native button with aria-pressed reflecting selection; controls support Tab/Enter/Space, visible focus, disabled state and unchanged click handlers.
Compact metric rows and search/target/action toolbar are unchanged, with no horizontal overflow for selector at 320px, 768px or 1280px.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Focused regression verifies both selectors render a shared SegmentedChoice with distinct selected/inactive CSS tokens, selected indicator, and hover state.
Regression verifies aria-pressed, button semantics, focus-visible contrast, target and mode handlers and disabled propagation.
Regression checks retained search and metrics layout; Chromium visual fixture inspects selectors at 320/768/1280 and validates classes in distributed Hermes CSS.

invariants.statement: All data loading, memory selection, navigation, editing, compaction and REST logic remain unchanged.
No modifications outside desktop/plugin.js and tests/test_desktop.py; no new runtime dependencies.
Prior compact metrics and toolbar remain in place.

forbidden_states.statement: Active and inactive options are visually indistinguishable.
Selected state is conveyed only by color, without accessible state or visual shape/indicator.
Selectors clip or cause horizontal scrolling on narrow windows.
The profile mariupol is updated or runtime behavior changes.

inputs.statement: Clean git HEAD 90d83b2db952133ee0c61903d930e26bebbd1109 and current two selector implementations.

outputs.statement: Shared SegmentedChoice and both selector uses in desktop/plugin.js.
Regressions and strict POLIS build proof.

failure_semantics.statement: Missing target percentages use existing 0% fallback; controls retain prior disabled behavior.
Failure of regression, CSS compatibility or Hermes validation blocks installation.
